findings.area: release process evidence / phase gate verification (phases 1-3)
findings.description: Phases 1, 2, and 3 claimed met Gates 1, 2, and 3, but there is no independent phase-review record for any of them: docs/implementation/phase-1/, phase-2/, and phase-3/ do not exist and contain no phase-review.json, and no per-task worker/reviewer reports exist for phases 1-3 (the report-persistence workflow starts at docs/implementation/4.6). Their gate claims rest on docs/changelog.md phase sections, PLANS.md acceptance-criteria checkboxes, tags v0.1.0-phase1..3, and the accumulated test-suite counts, none of which were independently audited at the time. This is a process/evidence gap, not a demonstrated correctness defect: the integrated behaviour those phases produce (plugin load, configuration boundary, provider reads, matching, state boundary) is exercised by the later phases, by the full test suite, and by this release audit's independent live end-to-end run.
evidence: git ls-files docs/implementation/phase-4 docs/implementation/phase-5 docs/implementation/phase-6 docs/implementation/phase-7 -> phase-review.json present, no phase-1..3 equivalents
docs/changelog.md Phase 1-3 sections record build/test results (Phase 1 43 tests; Phase 3 340 tests, 0 warnings/0 errors)
this audit: independent clean-export build/test (default 1218/60/1278; host-guarded 1234/44/1278) and live end-to-end run on the pinned host
findings.recommended_action: Reconcile the phase 1-3 gate claims with a retrospective evidence note, or record explicitly in docs/implementation-readiness.md that phases 1-3 predate the phase-review workflow and are covered by the later integrated reviews. No code action. Accepted for this release.

A residual unqualified phrase survives in task-level status paragraphs: PLANS.md lines 2481-2482 (task 7.3), 2620-2623 (task 7.3 superseded note), 2697 (task 7.8), and docs/changelog.md line 2207 (historical task 7.3 status). These are historical/status-narrative records, but the task 7.8 status line reads as a current claim that criterion 6 is fully met.

findings.description: The release archive is byte-reproducible (independently reproduced at the recorded SHA-256), but no automated test guards archive byte-identity: PluginPackagingTests asserts the entry set and the absence of a duplicate SkiaSharp runtime, not the archive bytes. Recorded as docs/limitations.md P1. A future regression in scripts/pack-release.cs or the build properties would not fail the suite.
evidence: this audit: clean-export ./build.sh package -> 567,856 bytes, bd10b9b6...
findings.recommended_action: Optional post-V1: add a packaging test that compares the produced archive SHA-256 to the recorded identity under the pinned SDK. Accepted for V1.

findings.description: ADR-012 states that every authentication failure returns a bounded 401 'with no body'; live requests return 401 with the ASP.NET Core [ApiController] framework application/problem+json body (type/title/status/traceId). Independently reproduced in this audit. No secret, header, candidate, or configuration detail is reflected, and the divergence is accurately documented in docs/limitations.md D1. Minor wording/behaviour gap for a future ADR-012 clarification.
evidence: live: wrong secret -> same 401 shape; candidate value absent from body (grep count 0)
findings.recommended_action: Track for a future ADR-012 clarification or suppress the framework body. Non-blocking; no leakage.

findings.description: ArtworkSubjectGate.Gates is a process-local static ConcurrentDictionary<string, SemaphoreSlim> keyed by item id + image surface with no idle eviction or LRU bound. Growth is bounded in practice by the distinct Jellyfin library items the host itself holds, is not attacker-controllable, and is not a log/state path. Recorded as docs/limitations.md D2 (task 7.4 finding 7.4-R1).
findings.recommended_action: Optional post-V1 idle eviction/LRU bound. Accepted for V1.

findings.description: No provider inventory/catalogue cache: every reconciliation work item re-reads the whole provider library and the per-record file resource, so the 'avoid unnecessary API requests' goal is only partially met for provider fetches. Independently observed live: unchanged-metadata re-runs still issued 5 provider requests even though no render or publication occurred. Render and publication are correctly fingerprint-gated. Recorded as docs/limitations.md F1.
evidence: live: unchanged re-run -> movie/episode image tags and served bytes identical, but 5 new mock requests (sonarr series/episode/episodeFile; radarr movie/moviefile)
findings.recommended_action: Deferred to Post-V1 (bounded short-TTL inventory cache and/or revision-token skip). Accepted for V1; it is the reason criterion 6 is partial.

findings.description: ConfigurationSnapshotService.TryReplace is implemented and validated but is not wired to Jellyfin's configuration-save path, so a saved webhook secret, provider enable/disable, badge/selector change, or limit change is not observed until process restart. Recorded as docs/limitations.md F2. All per-operation limit resolutions already read the current snapshot.
evidence: src/ArrTags/Configuration/ConfigurationSnapshotService.cs (TryReplace not called by a config-save subscriber)
this audit: configuration was applied by restart, which is the documented supported mechanism
findings.recommended_action: Tracked for Post-V1. Accepted for V1.

findings.description: No bounded, secret-free user-facing or diagnostic metrics/status surface exists, although the internal counters do. Documented as a recommendation, not a hard V1 gate (docs/limitations.md F3, architecture section 12).

Scheduled/post-scan/manual reconciliation enumerates from the start of a deterministic order, so a scope larger than QueueCapacity (default 512) covers only a bounded prefix and successive runs overlap rather than advancing. Recorded as docs/limitations.md F4. Event/webhook/per-item triggers are unaffected.
findings.recommended_action: Tracked for Post-V1. Accepted for V1.

findings.description: The tolerant ADR-010 non-canonical cross-runtime comparison requires a second explicitly selected non-canonical Linux runtime and its golden set; none is selected, so the comparison is skipped. Same-runtime golden and byte-determinism coverage passes. Recorded as docs/limitations.md V2.
evidence: RendererCrossRuntimeTests/NonCanonicalRuntimeFactAttribute skip in this audit's runs (default and host-guarded)
findings.recommended_action: Select and record a second runtime in a future milestone, or keep as an explicit environment limitation. Accepted for V1.

security_checked: Secrets never leak: 0 occurrences of the configured Sonarr/Radarr API keys or webhook secret in any host console log, the mock request log, plugin persisted state, or webhook HTTP responses. The values appear only in Jellyfin's PluginConfiguration file (ADR-005 design) and in docs as documented mock fixture values (RR-15).

Secret boundary: IPluginSecretResolver/SecretLease expose typed, version-matched leases; SecretLease.ToString excludes the value; API keys are applied only as X-Api-Key headers (never URL/query); webhook authentication uses CryptographicOperations.FixedTimeEquals with a 1024-char bounded candidate.
Authoritative state is never evicted as cache; invalid authoritative state is quarantined (live-reproduced) and invalid cache state is discarded.
Atomic writes: AtomicFileWriter uses a flushed temp file + File.Move(overwrite:true); StateEnvelopeCodec carries a schema version and SHA-256 payload integrity.

Lifecycle fence + write-ahead ordering: ArtworkPublisher re-reads the durable fence before writing Prepared, immediately before the image mutation, and before the final state commit (addresses the Phase 5 read-once MEDIUM); a complete operation is persisted before any Jellyfin image mutation.

Provider read-only: only HttpMethod.Get to /api/v3/system/status, /movie, /moviefile, /series, /episode, /episodeFile; no POST/PUT/DELETE to Arr services; webhooks never call Arr (live-verified 0 requests).

Boundedness: OperationalLimits.Validate enforces explicit ranges for queue (1-100000), provider/render concurrency, timeouts, retries/backoff, response bytes, webhook payload, artifact bytes, dimension pixels, batch size, freshness/retention, and quotas; live 413 confirmed for an oversized webhook body.

HTTP boundary authenticated and bounded: route /ArrTags/Webhook/{Sonarr,Radarr} is anonymous but shared-secret authenticated, constant-time, fail-closed, and reflects no sensitive detail (RR-5 covers the ProblemDetails-body wording gap only).
No secrets committed: git grep for the mock keys finds only documented test-fixture usages, not production credentials.
architecture_checked: ADR-001..ADR-013 unchanged and not contradicted by the implementation.

ADR-010 is honestly marked 'Accepted (partially superseded by ADR-015 ...)' in its status line and inline note; ADR-015 status records that it supersedes ADR-010's bundling parts; docs/research/skia-host-compatibility.md section 3 carries an explicit superseded marker and the F2 native byte-identity correction.

ADR-014 (state root ProgramDataPath/ArrTags via public BasePlugin.SetAttributes) coherent with ADR-002/003 and live-verified: no PluginsPath/ArrTags folder is created and the versioned install + relocated state survive restart.

ADR-015 coherent with the package: no managed/native SkiaSharp is shipped; the plugin shares the host's SkiaSharp through the default load context; live publication succeeds with no InvalidCastException/[FTL].
ADR-012 live behaviour matches the decision except the documented 'no body' wording (RR-5); ADR-013 provider ranges/optional-field policy match the committed fixtures and contract tests.

limitations_accepted: F1 / RR-7 - No provider inventory/catalogue cache; provider metadata is fetched per work item. Consequence: a large library performs one provider-library read per work item, so GOALS criterion 6 is only partially met for provider fetches. Evidence: docs/limitations.md F1; this audit observed 5 provider reads on an unchanged re-run that performed no render/publication.

F2 / RR-8 - Runtime configuration replacement is not wired to Jellyfin's save path. Consequence: secret/provider/badge/limit changes require a process restart. Evidence: docs/limitations.md F2; src/ArrTags/Configuration/ConfigurationSnapshotService.cs.
F3 / RR-9 - No bounded metrics/diagnostic-status surface. Consequence: no supported in-product view of queue depth/provider health. Evidence: docs/limitations.md F3; architecture section 12.

F4 / RR-10 - Reconciliation coverage is bounded by QueueCapacity. Consequence: a scope larger than 512 covers only a bounded prefix per run; event/webhook/per-item triggers unaffected. Evidence: docs/limitations.md F4; architecture lines 472-478.

F5 - Renderer depends on a host-supplied SkiaSharp with no bundled fallback. Consequence: a host without a compatible SkiaSharp fails closed (preserve current artwork); validated only on the pinned linux-musl-x64 Jellyfin 12.0.0 host; the plugin makes no RID-specific claim. Evidence: docs/limitations.md F5; ADR-015; live publication.

V1 - No live Sonarr/Radarr instance. Consequence: provider payload-shape variance beyond the committed fixtures is untested; contract-covered per ADR-013. Evidence: docs/limitations.md V1; mock fixture live run.

V2 / RR-11 - ADR-010 non-canonical cross-runtime comparison unselected/unrun. Consequence: the tolerant half of the ADR-010 strategy is an environment limitation; same-runtime golden/byte-determinism passes. Evidence: docs/limitations.md V2.
V3 / RR-12 - Jellyfin Enhanced coexistence is contract-level only. Consequence: live overlap/placement with Enhanced is unverified. Evidence: docs/limitations.md V3.

V4 / RR-13 - Automated live SaveImage read-back absent. Consequence: the live round trip is manual; the shipped artifact was live-verified in this audit and by the Phase 7 review. Evidence: docs/limitations.md V4; this audit's live served-vs-persisted identity match.

V5 / RR-14 - Live uninstall drain was previously unexercised; this audit exercised it successfully (204, install+state removed, artwork restored), narrowing the limitation to the automated coverage. Evidence: docs/limitations.md V5; this audit's authenticated uninstall.

V6 - Host-guarded facts are skipped without the pinned host. Consequence: the default ./build.sh test does not exercise the real host discovery/route/native-render paths; the host-guarded and forced-native runs do. Evidence: docs/limitations.md V6; this audit's three-suite matrix.

P1 / RR-4 - Byte-reproducibility depends on the pinned toolchain and has no automated byte-identity guard. Consequence: a different SDK could change bytes; a packer/build-property regression would not fail the suite. Evidence: docs/limitations.md P1; this audit's independent reproduction.
P2 / RR-16 - Reduced debug metadata for reproducibility. Consequence: harder source-level debugging of the released assembly; no runtime impact. Evidence: docs/limitations.md P2.

P3 - PackagePlugin=true stages but does not write the archive; ./build.sh package is the entry point. Consequence: direct MSBuild invocation must be followed by the packer. Evidence: docs/limitations.md P3.
P4 / RR-17 - SkiaSharp license notices ship although SkiaSharp is not redistributed. Consequence: extra attribution files only. Evidence: docs/limitations.md P4; ADR-015.

P5 / RR-18 - Pre-release orphaned state/uninstall-drain retention. Consequence: an unreleased developer install must delete PluginsPath/ArrTags once; an incomplete drain retains the relocated state root by design. Evidence: docs/limitations.md P5; ADR-014.

D1 / RR-5 - Webhook 401 body differs from ADR-012's 'no body' text (ProblemDetails type/title/status/traceId). Consequence: cosmetic wording gap; no sensitive detail reflected. Evidence: docs/limitations.md D1; this audit's live 401 responses.

D2 / RR-6 - ArtworkSubjectGate has no idle eviction. Consequence: one semaphore retained per distinct (item, surface) for process lifetime; bounded in practice and not attacker-controllable. Evidence: docs/limitations.md D2.

RR-1 - Phases 1-3 lack independent phase-review records. Consequence: their gate claims rest on changelog/PLANS evidence rather than a contemporaneous independent review; the integrated behaviour is covered by later phases and this audit. Evidence: absence of docs/implementation/phase-1..3 review files; this audit's full suite and live run.

RR-3 - Stale linux-x64 label in docs/implementation-readiness.md line 362. Consequence: imprecise host RID in one non-status surface. Evidence: docs/implementation-readiness.md:362.
RR-15 - Documented mock fixture API keys in tracked docs. Consequence: none; test-only values, never production credentials. Evidence: docs/testing/jellyfin-12-musl-test-host.md:173-174.

summary: ArrTags 0.1.0 is ready to ship with accepted, recorded limitations. The release candidate is frozen at HEAD 040ea0dd405b60dd8ea4990b5c9d4cc8b2ce8edb (clean tree, main +14, phase tags v0.1.0-phase1..7). I independently reproduced the release artifact from a clean git-archive export: it is byte-identical to the recorded identity (567,856 bytes, SHA-256 bd10b9b6bf5d31049082d27625b18ba127eb6e2860a454fe2d3c35ccebaaee51, 7 entries, every per-entry hash matched, manifest version 0.1.0.0 / targetAbi 12.0.0.0 / framework net10.0, no duplicate SkiaSharp/HarfBuzz runtime). The clean build reported 0 warnings / 0 errors; the default suite was 1218 passed / 60 skipped / 1278 total and the host-guarded suite 1234 / 44 / 1278 (both equal to the recorded baselines), and the forced-native suite was 1291 / 17 / 1308 with 0 failed and the native Skia facts unskipped. I exercised the packaged artifact end to end on the pinned Jellyfin 12.0.0 musl host: it installs and loads with no error (exactly one load, no plugin-context SkiaSharp), publishes badges through the real host IProviderManager.SaveImage with 0 [FTL], serves bytes whose SHA-256 equals the persisted ActiveImageIdentity, leaves the original source posters byte-unchanged, skips render/publication on unchanged metadata while republishing on changed metadata, stays up on a provider 503 with current artwork unchanged, survives a restart with the versioned install and relocated state preserved, restores the source on an authenticated uninstall (204), quarantines a corrupted authoritative record (integrity failure) without replaying or deleting it while preserving the served artwork, and enforces the authenticated/bounded webhook boundary (401/400/413/202, no secret reflected, no Arr calls). Both historical release blockers (7.2-F1 install-layout collision, 7.3-F1 duplicate-SkiaSharp fatal conflict) are independently confirmed fixed; no BLOCKER or HIGH finding remains open; all prior task/phase findings are resolved, accepted, or tracked. The only material residual is the partial GOALS criterion 6 (no provider catalogue cache, F1) plus the accepted verification/packaging limitations, all recorded in docs/limitations.md. One MEDIUM process gap (phases 1-3 lack independent phase-review records) and three LOW documentation-precision nits remain and are carried in this report; none affects the shipped behaviour. Decision: SHIP_WITH_ACCEPTED_LIMITATIONS.
